newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sees 1997 vehicle sales up at least 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sees 1997 vehicle sales up at least 27 pct.

text.p: Vehicle sales in Vietnam are likely to grow at least 27 percent this year from last year's 37,000 units, Deputy Minister for Industry Nguyen Xuan Chuan said on Tuesday.

He told Reuters that sales of vehicles assembled in Vietnam would rise sharply because the government quota for imports of new and second-hand complete built units (CBUs) had been cut to 20,000 this year from 30,000 in 1996.
"Last year, sales were about 23 percent higher than in 1995, so I would guess this year at least 27 percent higher," Chuan said.
He said cars accounted for around 35 percent of last year's total vehicle sales, but that share was now rising.

Chuan said the government had recently lifted an effective ban on imports of complete knock-down 1 (CKD1) kits which had been in place since the start of this year, setting a quota of 3,000 for the 14 vehicle makers licensed to operate in Vietnam.
Quotas on imports of CKD2s -- which unlike CKD1s are unwelded parts -- were scrapped with effect from this year.
Some of the seven carmakers now operating in Vietnam had said before the effective ban on CKD1 imports was lifted that they could be forced to slow or even halt production lines and lay off workers.
The government, anxious to localise the production of components, taxes CKD1 imports at a rate of 50 percent and CKD2 imports at a rate of 35 percent.
Producers are obliged to reach a rate of five percent of localised products in their first five years of operation and 30 percent after 10 years.
